label: copy-phase re-input of digit 1, plus the <DEL> step in short sequences
explanation: Never fires in the original phase. Almost all activation mass (95%) sits on two kinds of step: copy-phase steps where the fed-back input is the digit 1 (50% of mass), and the <DEL> step (45%). Both are only sparsely active. Only ~15% of copy-phase 1 inputs fire, and those that do are mostly early in the copy, especially when the 1 was the first original token (the top activations are sequences that start with 1). Activation weakens for later or repeated 1s. The <DEL> step fires on just 6% of sequences, more often when L is 3-4 and when the first token to output is p, r, 1, j or k. Other copy-phase inputs (f, p, n, ...) give only small residual activation. Precision is low because the gating conditions are graded and lexical, and no simple predicate captures them.
